chapter_theme: The lingam of knowledge (ஞான லிங்கம்): the supreme Siva takes form, formlessness and form-with-formlessness, the nine forms with Sadasiva in the middle, and comes as guru to souls; with him stands Parashakti, and the whole world is the play of Shakti and Siva, which enters the mind and makes it Siva.
structure_note: The chapter moves from the Lord's forms (1763 to 1765) through worship and the Lord's oneness with Shakti (1766 to 1770) to the world and the soul as the play of Shakti and Siva (1771, 1772).

1763.reading: The supreme Siva, who takes form, formlessness and form joined with formlessness, stands for the many souls with the purpose of being their guru too, and Sadasiva gives like the wishing tree.
1763.nuance: உருவும் அருவும் உருவோடு அருவும் (form, the formless, and form with the formless) is the Siddhanta division of the Lord's nine manifestations, set out in the next verse. தரு is taken as the wishing tree of the gods (karpaka).

1764.reading: The four below are form, the four above are formless, and the one in the middle, standing among them, is form and formless; these are his parts, and they are the supreme Siva himself.
1764.nuance: The verse gives only the numbers. Tradition names the four forms as Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra and Mahesvara, the four formless as bindu, nada, Shakti and Siva, and the middle as Sadasiva, who is worshipped as the lingam; 1776 lists the same nine.

1765.reading: Those who bow to him as the lord of the gods, the lord of the four-faced one, the lord of the four, Nandi who stands in the middle, saying 'lord of whom?', find by that path that the Great One is the lord of all at whose feet they are.
1765.nuance: நால்வர் (the four) is traditionally Sanaka and the three other sages taught by Siva as Dakshinamurti. ஏவர் பிரான் என்று is ambiguous: a question, or an exclamation ('lord of every one!').

1766.reading: I stood longing and worshipped so that my deeds would leave me; whether the Virgin is known together with the visible one who measures out the year, the month and the day, or the kindled one changes, it is one.
1766.nuance: The second half is obscure. The one who measures years, months and days is perhaps the sun, or the Lord as time; கன்னி (the Virgin) is taken as Shakti; மூண்டகை மாறினும் is unclear. The last words, that it is one, suggest the Lord and Shakti are one under every form.

1767.reading: The first, supreme God, the good God of the cosmos, the great God whom the devotees of light follow, the great God within justice, the stainless one, our Lord: Parashakti abides in his half.
1767.nuance: The list of epithets ends by placing Parashakti in the Lord's half (பாதியுள்), the image of Siva as half woman. சோதி அடியார் may be devotees who see the light, or the devotees of the one who is light.

1768.reading: Above Shakti is Parashakti, and within her is the pure state of Siva, an untouched clear light, beyond the beyond of the Father's holy feet; this is the truth of the Lord being himself, and it is also what accords.
1768.nuance: The grades Shakti, Parashakti and pure Siva state are technical. ஒத்தவும் ஆம் in the last line is unclear: perhaps that Siva and Shakti are equal, or that this matches the teaching.

1769.reading: If one sees the tip, the world appears; if one sees the place where it rises, one can abide; if one sees where it spreads, it is above Parvati; the one who saw it gather and rise is in my thought.
1769.nuance: கொழுந்து (tip, sprout or flame) has no stated subject. It may be the lingam's top, the flame of light in yoga, or kundalini rising; பார்ப்பதி மேலே may mean above Parvati or above what is seen. A symbolic reading is the only one that makes sense here.

1770.reading: Speaking first of the union of my Father, the Supreme, and my Mother, and then telling it in order, is jnana; he set the great-eyed one above the navel at the place where they met, and dwelt there rejoicing.
1770.nuance: பெருங் கண்ணி (the great-eyed woman, Shakti, or a great garland) and உந்தியின் மேல் (above the navel, a centre of the yogic body) are taken symbolically; tradition reads it as the Lord holding Shakti in a bodily centre.

1771.reading: In the play of Shakti and Siva, becoming life and feeding it amid the joined two mayas, then separating out the pure turiya, it enters the mind and makes the self Siva.
1771.nuance: இருமாயா is taken as pure and impure maya; துரியம் is the fourth state of consciousness. The subject that becomes life and enters the mind is unstated: the play, or Shakti and Siva.

1772.reading: The earth is the play of Shakti and Siva; Shakti becomes Siva and Siva becomes Shakti; there is no fixed thing other than Shakti and Siva, and it is always Shakti who takes shape as form.
1772.nuance: தாபரம் here can mean the fixed world or the installed lingam, as in 1755; both readings say the same: nothing stands apart from Shakti and Siva. The last line gives form to Shakti, leaving Siva formless.

links.note: 1764 counts four forms, four formless and one in the middle without naming them; 1776 names nine: Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra, Mahesa, the five-faced one, bindu, nada, Shakti and Siva, and calls them the lingam.
Both make Shakti with Siva the தாபரம்: 1755 of the installed lingam, 1772 of everything fixed, with no other.

source_issues: 1766: lines 2 to 4 (காண்டகை, கன்னி, மூண்டகை) are obscure.
1769: the subject of கொழுந்து is not stated and the verse may be incomplete in sense.
